supporting_dossier_passage: Section 8.1 states coverage (full text, selective appendices, code inspected read-only for named comparators) and that identities were verified before use.

supporting_dossier_passage: Saturation statement: the 12 close candidates came from the targeted search; known gaps: F01-F35 coding was not performed for new candidates, only the four Q1 elements were coded.

sentence_text: A-MAC admits an extracted candidate when a weighted feature score reaches a threshold, and it describes an update path that removes a conflicting memory and inserts a merged one \citep{arxiv_2603_04549}.
supporting_dossier_passage: Actual method: S(m) weighted sum, admit if S>=theta; Algorithm 1 removes the conflicting memory and inserts Merge(m, m_conflict). Limitations note the conflict path is absent from released code, hence 'describes'.

sentence_text: SSGM proposes a write validation gate that rejects proposed changes contradicting protected core facts, as a conceptual architecture without an implementation \citep{arxiv_2603_11768}.
supporting_dossier_passage: Actual method: Write Validation Gate G_write rejects deltas contradicting protected core facts; Exact scientific object: conceptual architecture, 'explicitly not a software implementation'; Evaluation: None.

sentence_text: Persona commits a tentative persona update only when a specification checker finds no hard violation, and otherwise rolls back to the last verified state \citep{persona_symmetry_2026}.
supporting_dossier_passage: Actual method: 'commit only if no hard violation, otherwise roll back to the last verified state'.

sentence_text: Memory-R1 trains a manager over ADD, UPDATE, DELETE and NOOP operations, and a MemGuard framework for memory contamination assigns ADD, UPDATE or SKIP to each memory atom \citep{arxiv_2508_19828,arxiv_2605_28009}.
supporting_dossier_passage: Memory-R1 scientific object: RL-fine-tuned memory manager (ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP). MemGuard-contamination method: each atom assigned one write operation in {ADD, UPDATE, SKIP}.

sentence_text: The CUPMEM prototype in STALE adjudicates whether a stored state is kept, archived, replaced or marked as unknown \citep{arxiv_2605_06527}.
supporting_dossier_passage: Method: LLM adjudicator decides whether an old state is kept, archived as STALE, replaced, or its slot marked UNKNOWN_CURRENT.

sentence_text: Persona (rollback) and A-MAC (rejection) implement no-commit outcomes, whereas the unknown marker in CUPMEM is itself a write, a deferred candidate in TARL enters a pending ledger, and MemTX records quarantined candidates with a reason \citep{persona_symmetry_2026,arxiv_2603_04549,arxiv_2605_06527,arxiv_2608_03699,arxiv_2607_23929}.
supporting_dossier_passage: Phase 8 section 8.4(b): Persona (rollback) and A-MAC (rejection) implement no-commit outcomes; Persona F06 note: rollback leaves persona state unchanged. STALE functional difference: UNKNOWN_CURRENT is a write of an uncertainty marker. TARL functional difference: defer_verify places the candidate in a Pending ledger (a state change). MemTX F06 note: non-commit outcomes recorded as QUARANTINED with a machine-readable reason rather than a pure no-op; Phase 8 section 8.3: quarantine is a state change.

sentence_text: Selective Memory$^{\dagger}$, When Not to Write Memory$^{\dagger}$ and MemReader$^{\dagger}$ also make write-time decisions with archive, needs-review and deferral outcomes \citep{arxiv_2603_15994,arxiv_2607_02579,arxiv_2604_07877}.
supporting_dossier_passage: SelectiveMemory: objects below the salience threshold are archived in cold storage. GovMem: routes each proposed write to PROMOTE, REJECT or NEEDS-REVIEW before long-term storage. MemReader: chooses to add, search, buffer (defer incomplete input) or ignore.

sentence_text: Graph-native cognitive memory keeps immutable revisions linked by SUPERSEDES edges and relates its revision operator to AGM belief-base postulates \citep{arxiv_2603_17244}.
supporting_dossier_passage: Actual method: append-only immutable Revision nodes, SUPERSEDES edge on revision; exact object: formal correspondence to AGM and Hansson belief-base postulates.

sentence_text: TOKI adjudicates contradictions with typed operators over a bitemporal fact table and writes the losing fact to an audit row \citep{arxiv_2606_06240}.
supporting_dossier_passage: Actual method: four typed operators over a dual-row bitemporal schema; each emits an audit row that keeps the losing fact.

sentence_text: SodaMem applies a deterministic slot rule that closes the older fact's validity interval and writes a SUPERSEDES edge \citep{arxiv_2608_08055}.
supporting_dossier_passage: Method: deterministic maintainer; older fact marked superseded, valid_until closed, SUPERSEDES edge written; functional difference: deterministic slot rule applied to every update-like fact.

sentence_text: GPM and the verifier-persisting MemGuard retain replaced records with supersedes links, and ECHO keeps a revision relation over typed bitemporal records \citep{arxiv_2608_12476,arxiv_2608_21867,arxiv_2608_21755}.
supporting_dossier_passage: GPM overlap: replacement via validated supersedes edge with append-only retained history. MemGuard-verifier overlap: replaced records retained as archived with supersedes/conflicts_with links. ECHO method: typed state records with revision relation; prior traces not erased.

sentence_text: In Governed Shared Memory a detector sets the supersedes link asynchronously after commit \citep{arxiv_2606_24535}, and in MemTX the superseded record has no successor-to-predecessor edge in code \citep{arxiv_2607_23929}.
supporting_dossier_passage: GovernedSharedMemory method: post-commit asynchronous contradiction detector sets supersedes_id on the newer row. MemTX F14 note: supersession marks the old record without a successor-to-predecessor edge in code.

sentence_text: Adjacent works concern revocation of stored precedents \citep{arxiv_2608_07429}, eviction after unconditional storage \citep{arxiv_2606_03463}, or the memory-update gap \citep{arxiv_2606_27472}.
supporting_dossier_passage: TEPA object: revocable keyed-precedent memory that removes contradicted precedents from retrieval and archives them. DMF functional difference: every interaction is stored; the deterministic rule governs eviction and retrieval suppression, not admission. Supersede object: diagnosis of the memory-update gap and an RL reward; classified ADJACENT.

sentence_text: MemTX stages beliefs through a fixed lifecycle with ordered commit checks and machine-checked invariants \citep{arxiv_2607_23929}.
supporting_dossier_passage: Actual method: eight-state belief lifecycle with fixed transition relation, four ordered commit checks, invariants checked by property-based testing and bounded exhaustive enumeration; Overlap with ASK: 'validated transitions and machine-checked invariants'.

sentence_text: TARL separates a learned action predictor from a deterministic executor that acts on accepted, pending and rejected ledgers \citep{arxiv_2608_03699}.
supporting_dossier_passage: Actual method: five executable actions over Accepted, Pending and History/Rejected ledgers; learned predictor; deterministic executor applies the selected action.

sentence_text: Quipu stores signed allow, deny and unknown verdicts with an evidence hash and replays recorded decisions as of a past instant, with a stated limit for denials \citep{arxiv_2608_16813}.
supporting_dossier_passage: Actual method: allow/deny/unknown verdicts are signed (ed25519), carry an evidence hash, and rules are versioned for as-of replay; Overlap: as-of decision replay with an explicitly bounded scope for denials (limitations: denials replay as attestation checks, not re-derivations).

sentence_text: The Log is the Agent derives graph state from an append-only event log and distinguishes strict from permissive replay, but it does not govern memory writes \citep{arxiv_2605_21997}.
supporting_dossier_passage: Actual method: append-only event log is source of truth, strict replay re-fires behaviors, permissive replay serves cached responses; functional difference: no memory write governance.

sentence_text: ESAA$^{\dagger}$ replays a hash-verified event log, MemLineage$^{\dagger}$ stores per-write source and context hashes in a Merkle log, and SuperLocalMemory 4.0$^{\dagger}$ writes a hash-chained audit trail atomically with the fact row \citep{arxiv_2602_23193,arxiv_2605_14421,arxiv_2608_08253}.
supporting_dossier_passage: ESAA: replay verification with hashing over an append-only event log. MemLineage: per-write SHA-256 of source data and of write-time context, RFC 6962 Merkle log. SuperLocalMemory4 overlap: per-write receipts and hash-chained audit persisted atomically with the fact row.

sentence_text: MGP specifies a storage-independent and runtime-independent protocol for governed memory writes, with candidate objects, merge hints and an audit sink, and it leaves the write decision to the caller \citep{mgp_hkuds_2026}.
supporting_dossier_passage: Exact object and Actual method: HTTP protocol specification for governed persistent memory between runtimes and heterogeneous backends; MemoryCandidate with merge_hint; JSONL audit event. Functional difference: MGP standardizes the interface and leaves the write decision to the caller's merge_hint.

sentence_text: GPM binds policy and normalizer versions and the ledger head into its decision records for claim release \citep{arxiv_2608_12476}, and TOKI pins the decoder tuple that keys its stored judge log \citep{arxiv_2606_06240}.
supporting_dossier_passage: GPM method: release decision record binds claim-multiset digest, policy and normalizer versions, snapshots and head. TOKI F19: decoder tuple (prompt, seed, model version, temperature, tool-output hash) keys the judge log.

sentence_text: Eywa accepts an extracted fact only after checks against its source text and writes it with a link to immutable evidence \citep{arxiv_2605_30771}.
supporting_dossier_passage: Actual method: Tier 1 candidate facts validated by support overlap, hard-anchor, subject and polarity checks; validated facts written with a provenance link to evidence; Tier 0 evidence immutable.

sentence_text: Several close neighbors govern other objects: claim release (GPM), policy compliance of writes (Quipu), persona state (Persona), commit discipline for agent actions (MemTX) and read-time currentness (ECHO) \citep{arxiv_2608_12476,arxiv_2608_16813,persona_symmetry_2026,arxiv_2607_23929,arxiv_2608_21755}.
supporting_dossier_passage: Phase 8 section 8.4(a). Exact scientific object fields: GPM state semantics before an outgoing structured claim; Quipu policy-compliance verdicts; Persona persona state; MemTX commit discipline between memory writes and irreversible agent actions; ECHO read-time currentness authority (functional difference).

sentence_text: HaluMem separates extraction, update and question-answering evaluation and inspects stored memory directly \citep{arxiv_2511_03506}.
supporting_dossier_passage: Overlap with ASK: separates evaluation of extraction, update and downstream answers; inspects the system's stored memory directly.

sentence_text: MemOps supplies gold lifecycle operation traces but scores them through probe answers rather than against executed write actions or persisted state \citep{arxiv_2607_12893}, and MemTrace separates retrieval reach from evidence use \citep{arxiv_2606_17328}.
supporting_dossier_passage: MemOps functional difference: labels scored through probe answers rather than a system's executed write actions or persisted state. MemTrace overlap: separates retrieval reach from evidence use.

sentence_text: TARL provides human five-way action labels derived from long-memory benchmarks together with exact next-state accuracy \citep{arxiv_2608_03699}, and MCB is a synthetic benchmark of the decision to persist, use temporarily, verify or ask for clarification \citep{arxiv_2608_19564}.
supporting_dossier_passage: TARL evaluation: TARL-Mem with human five-way labels derived from HaluMem-hard, LoCoMo, LongMemEval; metrics include exact next-state accuracy. MCB object: synthetic benchmark for persist, ephemeral use, verify, or clarify.

sentence_text: CPB$^{\dagger}$ scores admission policies, including an explicit abstain action, against fixed gold actions, and MemTxn$^{\dagger}$ reports admission audit, state recovery and downstream F1 separately \citep{arxiv_2609_30813,arxiv_2607_27834}.
supporting_dossier_passage: CPB method/evaluation: PROMOTE, REQUEST EVIDENCE, KEEP PRIVATE or ABSTAIN scored against fixed gold actions on a frozen test split, with consumer answers graded separately. MemTxn evaluation: item-disjoint audit of write admission, controlled fault recovery, downstream F1 on MemoryAgentBench.

sentence_text: Within a documented review of 30 full-text comparators, 12 search-surfaced candidates and 112 targeted search iterations, whose search record is released, we did not identify a system for persistent LLM-agent memory that implements all of the following: a three-way preserve, replace or abstain write decision whose abstention leaves state unchanged; lineage-preserving replacement; per-decision configuration and evidence identity; a declared replay scope; and separate reporting of action-label and downstream evidence.
supporting_dossier_passage: Section 8.5(2), wording adapted only: counts 30, 12 and 112 and the five-part conjunction are kept; 'no system was found' rendered as 'we did not identify'. Saturation statement: 112 discovery iterations plus 6 identifier-resolution steps recorded in SEARCH_LOG.csv.

sentence_text: This is a bounded result relative to the documented search iterations and not a claim that no such system exists.
supporting_dossier_passage: Section 8.5(2): 'a bounded negative search result relative to documented iterations, not an absence claim'; saturation statement: claimed only relative to documented iterations.
